ai.definition: A thermal energy storage system that uses sand to store and release heat, primarily intended for seasonal district heating.
ai.howItWorks: Surplus renewable electricity heats sand in insulated silos. The heated sand stores the thermal energy, which can be released later as needed for district heating purposes.
ai.problemSolved: Integrating intermittent renewable sources into a stable and reliable grid by providing long-term storage of heat from excess energy production.
ai.manufacturing: The process involves sourcing sand, insulating silos, installing heaters, and setting up monitoring systems to ensure efficient operation.
ai.buildProcess: Initial setup includes site preparation for the silos, installation of heating elements, insulation, and integration with renewable power generation sources. Ongoing processes involve regular maintenance and optimization of thermal transfer efficiency.
ai.costDrivers: Material costs (sand), energy consumption during charging, insulation quality, and operational maintenance expenses.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: The technology is currently in a pilot phase to validate its performance and economic viability before wider deployment.
ai.regulation: Regulatory frameworks for thermal storage are nascent; specific regulations may vary by region, but general policies on renewable energy integration could support this technology.
ai.risks: Technical risks include heat loss through insulation, potential degradation of materials over time, and the need for efficient heat transfer mechanisms. Economic risks involve the cost-effectiveness compared to other storage technologies and market acceptance.
ai.profitability: Profitability is uncertain at present due to pilot stage and variable costs; success depends on scaling and cost reduction strategies.
ai.futureDevelopment: Further research could focus on improving material properties, reducing heat loss, and optimizing system integration with renewable energy sources. Economic models will be crucial for long-term viability.

glossary.def: The process of storing heat generated from one time period to use it during another, typically to balance the supply and demand of energy.
Electricity derived from sustainable sources such as solar, wind, or hydro power that can be replenished naturally over short periods of time.

subsystems.name: Storage medium
subsystems.role: holds heat in a cheap, stable material that can cycle for decades.

subsystems.name: Electric heating
subsystems.role: converts surplus electricity into heat inside the store.

subsystems.name: Insulated silo
subsystems.role: contains the sand and minimises heat loss over weeks or months.

subsystems.name: Heat transfer and discharge
subsystems.role: moves heat into and out of the sand and delivers it to a heat network.
parts: piping to district heating or process load

subsystems.name: Controls and monitoring
subsystems.role: manages charge and discharge cycles, temperatures and safety.

buildSteps.title: Size and site the store
buildSteps.detail: Choose a location beside an existing district heating network or industrial heat load, and size the silo for the required megawatt-hours and discharge rate.

buildSteps.title: Build the insulated container
buildSteps.detail: Pour a concrete base, erect a steel or concrete shell, and line it with thick high-temperature insulation to keep losses low.

buildSteps.title: Install internal air channels
buildSteps.detail: Fit pipes or ducts that distribute air through the sand bed so heat can be charged and later extracted evenly.

buildSteps.title: Install electric heaters
buildSteps.detail: Mount resistive elements or electrodes that will heat the sand to several hundred degrees Celsius, often around 500–600 °C.

buildSteps.title: Connect power and controls
buildSteps.detail: Wire the heaters through transformers and switchgear, and install sensors and control software to manage charging from the grid.

buildSteps.title: Fill with sand
buildSteps.detail: Load clean, dry sand of a suitable grain size, compact it, and seal the container.

buildSteps.title: Commission and connect
buildSteps.detail: Heat the store for the first time, test charge and discharge cycles, and link the heat exchanger to the district heating or process system.

buildSteps.title: Operate
buildSteps.detail: Charge when electricity is cheap or abundant, and discharge heat when demand peaks or when renewable supply is low.

prerequisites.why: the economics depend on charging when power is otherwise curtailed or low-cost.
they provide a ready customer for large volumes of low- to medium-temperature heat.
long-duration storage only works if heat loss over weeks is small.
simple, proven and efficient at turning electricity into heat.
predicting seasonal losses and cycling behaviour in large sand beds is still being validated.

pathway.milestone: pilot plants supplying district heat, including in Finland
pathway.unlocks: real operating data on efficiency, losses and cycling.

pathway.milestone: commercial plants of tens to hundreds of megawatt-hours connected to city heat networks
pathway.unlocks: displacing fossil fuels for winter heating at scale.

pathway.milestone: integration with industrial process heat for drying, food processing and chemicals
pathway.unlocks: clean heat for factories that cannot easily electrify directly.

pathway.milestone: city-scale seasonal storage, potentially paired with power generation
pathway.unlocks: storing summer solar or wind for winter demand, reducing the need for backup fuels.
